record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Find characterizations, not phrased in terms of operators, of real Banach spaces whose numerical index is 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Find characterizations of Banach spaces with numerical index 0 which do not involve operators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with norm $\|\cdot\|$ and topological dual $X^*$. For a bounded linear operator $T: X \to X$, define its numerical radius by
$$v(T) := \sup\{|x^*(T x)| : x \in X,\ x^* \in X^*,\ \|x\| = \|x^*\| = x^*(x) = 1\}.$$
The numerical index of $X$ is the constant
$$n(X) := \inf\{v(T) : T \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \|T\| = 1\} \in [0,1].$$
Equivalently, $n(X)$ is the greatest constant $k \geq 0$ such that $k\|T\| \leq v(T)$ for every bounded linear operator $T$ on $X$.

Find a characterization of those real Banach spaces $X$ satisfying $n(X) = 0$ that is expressed purely in terms of the geometry of $X$ (its norm, unit ball, or related geometric structures), without referring to bounded linear operators, their norms, or their numerical ranges.
artifact.status_search_result: A search of the literature on the numerical index of Banach spaces produced a number of geometric results (e.g., on lush spaces and characterizations connected with numerical index one), but no operator-free geometric characterization of real Banach spaces with numerical index zero. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of Banach spaces with numerical index one
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric characterizations are discussed mainly for numerical index one, extending McGregor's characterization, with no operator-free characterization given for n(X)=0.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on geometric characterizations for n(X)=1, not n(X)=0.

status_evidence.title: Positive and negative results on the numerical index of Banach spaces and duality
status_evidence.snippet: Results on renorming and duality of the numerical index; no operator-free characterization of n(X)=0 is provided.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to study n(X)=0 via operator-theoretic constructions.
